clinical_scope.population: Adults and young people aged 16 years or older unless otherwise specified by local protocol
excluded_populations: pediatric specialty pathways unless explicitly validated
clinical_scope.intended_use: High-risk candidate retrieval and guideline-based verification for suspected Acute Coronary Syndrome.
clinical_scope.important_boundary: This graph supports clinical reasoning and missed-diagnosis risk reduction; it is not an autonomous diagnostic system.

distinctions.description: ACS is a clinical syndrome of acute myocardial ischemia; AMI requires acute myocardial injury with ischemic evidence.

basic_info.working_definition: Acute coronary syndrome is a spectrum of acute myocardial ischemia that includes unstable angina, NSTEMI, and STEMI.
why_high_risk_for_missed_diagnosis: ACS can present with atypical symptoms or non-chest-pain equivalents.
Initial ECG may be nondiagnostic and troponin may be negative in unstable angina or early NSTEMI.
Mimics such as aortic dissection, pulmonary embolism, pericarditis, pneumothorax, and GI disorders may look similar.
A missed STEMI or high-risk NSTEMI can lead to preventable myocardial damage, shock, arrhythmia, or death.
basic_info.time_sensitivity: Requires rapid ECG, serial troponin, risk stratification, and immediate reperfusion pathway if STEMI is identified.
do_not_use_as: a rule-out tool from symptoms alone

case_input_normalization.single_pass_missing_information_policy: Do not ask follow-up questions. Mark missing critical information explicitly and state how missingness affects verification.
case_input_normalization.normalization_patch_note: Normalization rules were systematized on 2026-06-28 to support retrieval from textual triggers, abbreviations, and numeric clinical facts. Rules map common case expressions to graph node ids where available. They are retrieval signals, not autonomous diagnostic criteria.

graph_nodes.name: Chest pressure, heaviness, tightness, or pain
Pain radiating to arm, jaw, neck, shoulder, back, or epigastrium
12-lead ECG within 10 minutes when ACS suspected
Risk score or structured risk assessment
Chest imaging when alternative diagnosis possible
Echocardiography when unstable or diagnosis unclear
Dynamic ST depression or T-wave inversion
Normal troponin with ischemic symptoms consistent with unstable angina
Immediate STEMI reperfusion pathway when indicated
High-risk NSTE-ACS invasive evaluation when indicated

activation_logic.minimum_activation: Chest pain or ischemic equivalent plus ECG/troponin/risk context, or unexplained acute cardiopulmonary instability.

strong_activation_patterns.reason: Objective ECG evidence raises ACS priority.
Suggests MI within ACS spectrum when ischemic evidence present.
Possible unstable angina; cannot be dismissed by normal troponin alone.

case_features: isolated fatigue or nausea without risk context

symptom_to_candidate_retrieval.scoring_warning: Weights are for retrieval and explanation only. They are not calibrated probabilities and must not be used as a diagnostic score.

guideline_verification_pathway.check: Does the presentation suggest acute myocardial ischemia or an ischemic equivalent?
guideline_verification_pathway.positive_result: Proceed to immediate ECG and troponin pathway.
guideline_verification_pathway.negative_result: Lower priority but continue if atypical high-risk presentation.
guideline_verification_pathway.if_missing: Cannot characterize ACS likelihood without symptom onset/quality and risk context.

guideline_verification_pathway.check: Does ECG show STEMI, STEMI-equivalent, NSTE-ACS ischemic changes, or nondiagnostic findings?
guideline_verification_pathway.positive_result: Classify ACS subtype and pathway urgency.
guideline_verification_pathway.negative_result: Repeat ECG if symptoms persist or suspicion remains.

guideline_verification_pathway.check: Are serial high-sensitivity troponins available and interpretable?
guideline_verification_pathway.positive_result: Differentiate AMI from unstable angina or nonischemic injury.
guideline_verification_pathway.negative_result: Normal serial troponins lower MI probability but do not automatically exclude unstable angina.
guideline_verification_pathway.if_missing: Serial troponin data missing or timed too early.

guideline_verification_pathway.check: Is the case STEMI, NSTEMI, unstable angina, nonischemic injury, or uncertain?
Are there high-risk features such as instability, recurrent ischemia, heart failure, arrhythmia, or dynamic ECG/troponin?
guideline_verification_pathway.positive_result: Escalate ACS priority and management pathway.

guideline_verification_pathway.check: Are dissection, PE, pericarditis, pneumothorax, esophageal rupture, or abdominal emergencies plausible?
guideline_verification_pathway.negative_result: ACS remains primary if ECG/troponin evidence aligns.

distinguishing_features: Troponin rise/fall plus ischemic evidence places the case in AMI subset.
Abrupt tearing pain, neurologic deficit, pulse/BP differential, aortic regurgitation, shock.
Dyspnea, pleuritic chest pain, hypoxemia, syncope, VTE risk factors.
Pleuritic positional pain, diffuse ST elevation, PR depression, viral prodrome.
Unilateral pleuritic pain, dyspnea, reduced breath sounds.
Epigastric/right upper quadrant pain, meal association, abnormal liver/pancreatic enzymes.

final_assessment.safety_statement: Clinical decision support only; urgent clinician assessment is required when a high-risk condition is suspected.

evidence_sources.title: 2025 ACC/AHA/ACEP/NAEMSP/SCAI Guideline for the Management of Patients With Acute Coronary Syndromes
evidence_sources.publisher: American College of Cardiology / American Heart Association and partner societies
key_points: Addresses acute management across unstable angina, NSTEMI, and STEMI.
Supports rapid ECG-based classification, serial cardiac troponin evaluation, risk stratification, and timely reperfusion or invasive management when indicated.

evidence_sources.title: 2023 ESC Guidelines for the management of acute coronary syndromes
key_points: Provides an integrated guideline for patients presenting with acute coronary syndrome across the spectrum of STEMI and NSTE-ACS.
Used here for diagnostic classification and high-risk ACS verification logic.

evidence_sources.title: Fourth Universal Definition of Myocardial Infarction (2018)
key_points: Myocardial infarction requires acute myocardial injury detected by cardiac troponin rise and/or fall plus clinical evidence of acute myocardial ischemia.
Acute myocardial injury without ischemic evidence should not automatically be labeled myocardial infarction.

must_not: Do not make an autonomous definitive diagnosis.
Do not use a single symptom, sign, laboratory result, score, or imaging clue as a standalone rule-in or rule-out criterion.
Do not provide patient-facing reassurance when critical red-flag data are missing.
Do not ignore competing high-risk differential diagnoses.
Do not replace local emergency, specialty, or hospital protocols.
Do not generate medication orders; recommend clinician-led pathway activation instead.
Do not exclude ACS based on normal first ECG or early troponin alone.
Do not label unstable angina as benign.
must_do: Use this graph for candidate retrieval, missed-diagnosis risk reduction, and guideline-based verification.
Separate supporting evidence, evidence against, and missing critical information.
State whether verification is complete, partial, impossible from available data, or contradicted.
Include differential diagnoses that can mimic the condition.
Trace guideline-dependent claims to evidence IDs.
Mark output as clinical decision support requiring qualified clinician review.
Always classify into STEMI/NSTEMI/unstable angina/uncertain/nonischemic injury when data allow.
